messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

The house matters to me as a chance to build financial independence with my husband. I’d like to buy it at a family discount, but that isn’t settled, and C hasn’t agreed. A possible NCE is: “I want to feel secure and able to make independent choices.” That wording fits; my well-being is why it matters. I have no discomfort with starting this way.

I’d like my wish to use some money to start a dance studio to be heard as my own; that matters to me because it’s the only way I can see to make it happen. I’m not sure yet what wording fits best. No particular discomfort with starting this way.

I want a fair financial share, and I haven’t agreed to subsidize A and her husband’s discounted purchase. I care about A, but that doesn’t make the arrangement fair; the price and shares aren’t settled. B should speak for herself—I want her needs heard, but I can’t decide for her. I’m not in a hurry, and I’m not holding back. No discomfort with this process from me.

That wording mostly fits; I’d like my hope of starting a dance studio to be heard in it too. Being younger isn’t a separate concern for me, and I’m not sure I feel caught in the middle. My needs matter, and I’m not holding back. This pace is okay.

#1 Fits: I want a fair share, not to subsidize A’s purchase. #2 Fits: I won’t sign unless I freely agree. #3 Fits: B should speak for herself. #6 Fits: A is my twin and I care about her, but fairness matters too. #7 Fits: I’m not in a hurry; I want clarity before anything is settled. I’m not holding back, and I’m comfortable with the drafts and pace.

#4 still fits. The twin draft fits for me too. I feel my needs matter, I’m not holding back, and I have no discomfort with the process. One small clarification: the twin item is listed as #9, though the message says it would be added as #10.

The revised wording fits. Being heard in my own words matters because my hope to start a dance studio is mine. I’m not sure whether feeling caught in the middle is a concern for me. My needs matter, I’m not holding back, and this pace is okay.
Being A’s twin matters because I care about her, but it isn’t separate from #6; use #6 wording only. My needs matter, I’m not holding back, and I’m comfortable with the list, draft, and pace.
I have no other concern, and I’m not holding back. No discomfort with the list or pace. I do still hope the possibility of buying the house with my husband can be considered, but nothing is settled.

I’m not sure what matters about it, so please leave #8 unresolved; I don’t want to call it a concern when I’m unsure. It feels safe enough to say that. My studio hope being heard is my concern; my needs matter, and this pace is okay.
I’ll share this with A and B; they need to answer for themselves. I’m comfortable with the pace, but I’m not choosing an option or agreeing to a purchase.
